title: Vow of Teeth

continuity_fixes: Ch 1 says Kettamala has 'one gate and a hundred and some soldiers'. Ch 24 and ch 29 give the garrison as sixty, and ch 14 uses an east postern, which is a second gate. FIX: In ch 1, change 'A fort with one gate and a hundred and some soldiers' to 'A fort with one great gate and sixty-odd soldiers'.

On the wedding night Neela lifts a bar off the shutters. Ch 10 (Janu), ch 16 and ch 30 all say the shutters were never barred before the wedding and Devan first barred them on the second dusk. FIX: In ch 1, replace 'with a bolt that slid back easily. She lifted the bar, eased the first shutter' with 'held only by an iron latch; the long teak bar hung unused on its hooks. She lifted the latch, eased the first shutter'.

Devan watches her 'lift the bar from the west shutters' on the wedding night, but the bar is first used on the second dusk (ch 3, ch 10, ch 30). FIX: In ch 2, change 'he watched her lift the bar from the west shutters' to 'he watched her lift the latch on the west shutters'.

Asha's parrot signature is 'a quick three-stroke bird, beak open'. Ch 12 describes it as five strokes with the beak always whole. FIX: In ch 2, change 'A quick three-stroke bird, beak open, always laughing at something' to 'A quick five-stroke bird with a whole beak, always laughing at something'.

Neela recalls leaving 'the bar propped against the wall' after the wedding night and finding it back in its brackets 'this morning'. No bar was used on night one, and Devan only bars the shutters at this chapter's dusk. FIX: In ch 3, replace the two sentences about last night's bar with: 'Last night there had been no bar across them at all. Tonight there was, and a man who barred a window looked at its bar.'

'Chinna snored on his mat'. Chinna is a woman: ch 1 calls her 'a broad woman', and ch 18 and ch 31 mention 'her bad hip'. FIX: In ch 4, change 'Chinna snored on his mat' to 'Chinna snored on her mat'.

Devan thinks 'Not once had she come to the bed', but ch 2 and ch 3 show her lying down in the bed with her back to him at each dawn. FIX: In ch 5, change 'Not once had she come to the bed' to 'Each time she had come to the bed shaking and lain with her back to him, as far off as the mattress allowed'.

In ch 4 Neela turns back in the yard at first light. Her clothes are in the chamber (she always leaves them on the sill), yet in ch 5 she walks up through the stair door, past the two west-stair guards, as a woman, and no one remarks on it. FIX: In ch 5, add that she came in 'with a saddle-blanket from the stable round her', so Devan hears the rough wool drop before the bed creaks.

'She had known him eight days' falls on the morning she counts thirty-four nights left, which is day 6. Ch 9 (thirty-two nights left) is the first point where 'eight days' fits. FIX: In ch 7, change 'eight days' to 'six days'.

Muthu says 'Tomorrow's the seventh day', but he made his seventh-day request in ch 5, only about three days earlier. FIX: In ch 8, change 'Tomorrow's the seventh day' to 'Four days to the seventh day'.

Devan's hand lies 'open on the blanket, palm up', yet Neela counts seven scars across the knuckles, which are on the back of the hand and can't be seen palm up. FIX: In ch 10, change 'palm up' to 'palm down, fingers loose'. Leave the later 'his hand still lay open on the blanket'.

Neela remembers that Janu said 'He used to have a partner' 'at the table, to the soup.' In ch 3 Janu said it standing at the lip of the kalari pit during the tour. FIX: In ch 11, change to: 'Janu had said it at the lip of this pit, on the first morning.'

Muthu claims his mother 'writes me every week' and Devan believes him. In ch 24 Devan already knows she writes once a month, and he would have caught the false claim. FIX: In ch 12, change 'She writes me every week, I answer once a month' to 'She writes me once a month, I answer once a month'.

Neela reasons from Asha's oilcloth token ('in a camphor chest, in a dead girl's room') and quotes Asha's note 'Need a second to be sure.' In ch 12 Devan folded the token and its note into his sleeve before Neela came into the room, and he never showed them to her. She has never smelled that wax or read that note. FIX: In ch 14, replace the Asha references with what she has seen herself: 'Janu's kitchen. The broken tally on the hall table, the day the patrol came in.' Change her reason to: 'The warden broke one tally open in the hall and said it wasn't enough. Here was a second, and he could have it.'

In ch 14 Neela weighs that going to the narrows leaves the meeting stone's cup empty a second night, after the fever night. Nothing shows her marking it later. Yet ch 16 says she has missed the stone only once ('the night of his fever'), and in ch 18 Ammu counts only the fever night plus the three bare nights of ch 16 to 17. The narrows night is missing from both counts. FIX: In ch 14, where she goes 'by the long way to the cleft in the rocks under the second spur', add one line: she passes the meeting stone first and drags her cheek across the cup, late but marked.

Neela recalls that 'the warden had broken one tally open in the hall and said it wasn't enough.' In ch 4 Devan says only that the wax is genuine council wax and never says one is not enough. The 'need a second' idea is Asha's note, which Neela has not seen. FIX: In ch 14, change the line to: 'The warden had broken one tally open in the hall. One tally was a story; two were a case.'

Neela recalls 'last night's supper' and the bowl-of-milk line. That supper was in ch 14, eight nights before the storm. FIX: In ch 15, change 'And last night's supper, over Janu's fish' to 'And that supper eight nights ago, over Janu's fish'.
The drop from the warden's window is called 'forty feet'. Ch 4 gives the wall under the window as thirty feet. FIX: In ch 15, change 'a drop of forty feet' to 'a drop of thirty feet'.

Neela recalls Janu's story as one about 'a leopard that took a bride' that Devan stopped with 'enough'. In ch 9 the story was a man-eating leopard taking a man above the second ford, and Devan said 'Not tonight, Janu'. FIX: In ch 16, change the sentence to 'Janu had told a story at supper once, of a man-eater of the pass that left a traveller's sandals on the road. Devan had said Not tonight, Janu, so mildly that she went red and stopped.'

Neela's reread says Devan stopped Janu's leopard story at supper by saying 'I'm tired of leopards, Janu,' mildly, 'by daylight.' In ch 9 Neela was at that supper and heard 'Not tonight, Janu.' Ch 30 places the 'tired of leopards' line later, in the kitchen, by day, out of Neela's hearing. Supper is also not daylight. FIX: In ch 16, change the line to: 'Janu was halfway through it over the rice when Devan said, "Not tonight, Janu." He said it quietly, with his eyes on his bowl.'

The reread puts the sentry first and has the hounds 'kennelled in the first week, after the sentry was pulled.' In fact the hounds were kennelled from the second night (the ch 3 night walk and Kannan in ch 4), before Devan pulled the sentry in ch 5. Ch 30 and F344 also give hounds first, sentry second. FIX: In ch 16, swap the order: the hounds kennelled from the second night, then 'the sentry above the window pulled a few nights on.' Delete 'after the sentry was pulled.'

Neela recalls that 'Janu had called it damp-madness.' In ch 10 Janu told her the damp theory belonged to Bhaskaran's lads, and that her own theory was 'shy.' F322 repeats the error. FIX: In ch 16, change to: 'Bhaskaran's lads called it damp-madness, Janu called it shyness, and Chinna ran a wager on it at the kitchen door.'

In ch 10 Janu gives the fort's theories about the barred shutters: Bhaskaran's lads say privacy, Gopan says Janu's old tale, Janu herself says the damp, and Chinna runs the wager. Ch 31 repeats that set (damp-madness, privacy, Janu's old tale). Ch 16 instead says Bhaskaran's lads called it damp-madness and Janu called it shyness. FIX: In ch 16, change the sentence to: 'Bhaskaran's lads called it privacy, Gopan called it Janu's old tale, Janu called it the damp, and Chinna ran a wager on it at the kitchen door.'

In ch 12 Sudhi rides 'with the palace green on his sleeve'. In ch 17 Devan says no one looks in the bag of 'a man in royal blue'. Blue is the registry courier's colour in ch 8, not Sudhi's. FIX: In ch 17, change 'a man in royal blue' to 'a man in palace green'.

Watching Muthu give Sudhi a grey-sealed letter, Neela notes 'She had seen it three times now.' She has never witnessed one before: the ch 12 handoff is in Devan's POV while she is at supper in the hall. FIX: In ch 17, change 'She had seen it three times now.' to 'It was the first time she had seen it, though Janu teased him about his mother's post.'

Ammu says she has written to Kirri 'eleven times'. In ch 7 she had written three letters, and the bible fixes the count at three (C08). FIX: In ch 18, change 'I've written eleven times to the address she gave' to 'I've written four times now to the address she gave'.

Ch 18 opens at sixteen nights and ends the same day at 'Fifteen nights.' Ch 19, the next evening, also says fifteen, so the count stalls for a day. FIX: In ch 18, change the closing 'Fifteen nights.' to 'Sixteen nights.'

continuity_fixes: 'Devan had closed the shutters himself before the light went, as he did each evening.' In ch 16 he promised the shutters were hers and that he would not touch them, and in ch 17 they stand open. FIX: In ch 20, change it to 'Neela had closed the shutters herself before the light went, slat by slat'.

Devan names the story that made him stop Janu as 'the one about the leopard that waits at the foot of the bed'. The story he stopped in ch 9 was the man-eater of the pass. Devan never lies. FIX: In ch 21, change it to 'the one about the man-eater of the pass that left a man's sandals on the road'.

Ammu says the watcher logs a night with no fresh scent-posts as refusal, and that a second gap back to back with the rain night is the one Chathu would act on. But ch 16 to 18 already had three consecutive bare nights (ch 17 'three nights'; Ammu in ch 18: 'Three nights, the cup was bare'). Under the same rule those would have been logged, and the book gives no cover and no consequence for them. FIX: In ch 22, add to Ammu's lines: 'Your three bare nights last week already went down. That's why he sent the sweets. Another run of gaps on top of the rain night is the one he'd act on.'

In ch 20 Devan leaves his grey stone on the sill and keeps Kannan's white pebble as his cheek stone ('Keep Kannan's. It's the clean one.'). In ch 22 he takes 'the grey pebble from his pouch'. FIX: In ch 22, change 'take the grey pebble from his pouch' to 'take the white pebble from his pouch'.

On reading the slip, Neela thinks of Ittan as 'the man who had proposed the match'. Nothing has shown her this. Only Devan knows Ittan's name stood first on the council letter (ch 23), and Ittan says it aloud only in ch 28. FIX: In ch 22, replace 'the man who had proposed the match' with 'the man whose letter had asked so warmly after the warden's bride'.

Neela 'had been in the room that night, on her side of the bed with her face to the wall, while he read the letter aloud to the dark'. In ch 17 he read Ittan's letter at noon by the west window, and they discussed it face to face. FIX: In ch 23, change it to 'She had stood by the chest while he read the letter aloud at the window at noon, and she had counted the friends in it'.

Neela's nightly countdown to the pass closing gives about eleven nights left on the ch 23 morning (fifteen at ch 19, then one fewer each day). Ch 23 says the pass is sealed 'in eight days', and Devan repeats 'Eight days to the seal.' Nobody notices the three-day gap, and up to ch 18 the book treats the count and the closing as the same date ('The pass shuts in sixteen days'). FIX: In ch 23, give Neela one line after 'eight days': 'Three days ahead of the rains. The council always seals early, and I've been counting to the rains, not the seal.'

Neela tells Devan Muthu should follow 'if I'm not back by the second dusk'. Her actual order in ch 26, which Chathu's timing depends on, is first light on the second day, meeting her on the wood road. FIX: In ch 25, change 'If I'm not back by the second dusk, he's to bring you after me' to 'If I'm not back by first light on the second day, he's to bring you up the wood road after me'.
Ammu says 'I wrote her every month', which would be about two dozen letters in two years. Ch 7 has three letters. FIX: In ch 27, change 'I wrote her every month' to 'I wrote her and wrote her'.

'She had never said it. Not in twenty-one years.' Her night-shape was fixed at her first turning at 16, eleven years ago. Twenty-one years is her time in the guild. FIX: In ch 27, change 'Not in twenty-one years' to 'Not in eleven years'.

Neela is 'on the wall by the cistern housing, where the sentry used to stand'. The cistern housing is on the east rampart (ch 19), but the pulled sentry walked the west rampart above the warden's window (ch 5). FIX: In ch 28, change it to 'on the west rampart above the chamber window, where the sentry used to stand'.

Ammu's Valli cloth and resin pouch are found in the roots of the tree where she died, 'cached there before dusk'. In ch 26 to 27, though, Ammu is in the kennel and yard with Neela right up to sunset, and she turns on the cook-house roof. She had no time to reach the tree line before dusk. FIX: In ch 28, change 'She had cached it there before dusk' to 'Muthu had found it at the cook-house corner, where she had shed it, and laid it at the tree.'

Devan reads the marriage-writ clause aloud as 'In the event of the warden's death in office, the pass-seal passes to his wife in trust...'. The same document's wording in ch 8 is '...and the said wife, being lawfully wed, shall hold the pass-seal of Kettamala in trust from the hour of the warden's death, until the council shall name another in his place.' FIX: In ch 29, replace the quoted clause with the ch 8 wording.

Devan says he left the shutters 'Open, as my father kept them' on the first night, but ch 1 and ch 2 show them closed, and Neela opens them herself. FIX: In ch 30, change 'Open, as my father kept them' to 'Shut on the latch and never barred, as my father kept them'.

Devan says she touched the base of his skull 'in the dark' in bed and lay down afterwards, and that he was afraid of her 'for about nine days'. The three-breath touch happened at dawn in the kalari while he drilled (ch 11, ch 12). In ch 17 he said his fear lasted 'about a breath'. FIX: In ch 30, move the scene to the pit: 'You came down the north steps while I drilled. You put your fingers at the base of my skull...you lifted your hand and told me my guard dropped on the left.' Change 'afraid' to 'wary' and 'nine days' to 'eleven days'. Have Neela answer 'You stopped breathing. I thought you were waiting for the blow.'

Devan says he stopped Janu's stories by asking her 'at the table, by day' and telling her he was 'tired of leopards', and that Neela 'weren't in the room'. In ch 9 he stopped the story at supper with Neela at the table, saying 'Not tonight, Janu'. FIX: In ch 30, change it to 'I stopped her at supper, you were there. Afterwards I told her in the kitchen, by day, that I was tired of leopards. You weren't in the kitchen.'

Devan says the hounds 'went to the kennel within a few nights' of the second dusk. Ch 3 (night two) already has them behind a kennel door, ch 4 says 'every night since your wedding', and ch 16 says 'from the second night'. FIX: In ch 30, change 'The hounds went to the kennel within a few nights, the sentry after them' to 'The hounds went to the kennel that same night, the sentry a few nights after.'

In ch 28 Neela waters the forty-one kennel animals once and says the troughs will be dry in three days. Devan orders Bhaskaran's men out the morning after the return. Ch 31 says 'Rain held the first run' and that Muthu goes three days after the vow, which leaves about eight days without water. Ch 32 then reports the animals, Kirri included, alive and settled, and no one mentions the gap. FIX: In ch 31, change 'Rain held the first run' to 'Bhaskaran's men got water through before the rain shut the wood road for a few days.' Keep Muthu's run as the second one.

errors: 10 continuity errors remain after 3 automatic fix round(s): ch 5: The bible says Devan never lies to Neela. In ch 5 he tells Neela and Kannan 'I have to see Bhaskaran about the gate', and the narration says 'It was not true.'; ch 8: Neela asks why Raiu was moved and Devan answers 'Oil.' The narration has already said 'It did not save oil.' That is a direct lie to Neela, which breaks his fixed voice rule. Ch 17 and ch 30 also rely on him never having lied to her.; ch 13: Chinna is a woman (ch 1 'a broad woman', ch 18, ch 21 'Chinna's got a bad hip', ch 31 'her bad hip'). In ch 13 Neela says 'Tell Chinna it's for the warden. He'll hurry.'; ch 14: In the supper scene, ch 14 reads 'Chinna at the kitchen door with his bad hip.' Chinna is a woman.; ch 17: Devan says that on the wedding night she 'slipped the latch like somebody who had done it before, carefully, so the slat wouldn't ring.' In ch 1 Neela leaned on the third slat on purpose to make it creak, and in ch 2 Devan's POV records that 'The third slat creaked.'; ch 20: Ch 20 calls Neela's lie that Devan 'thinks I'm a bride who sleeps badly' 'a first lie'. In ch 18 she had already lied to Ammu several times ('Nobody's seen', 'To learn his sleep', 'He sleeps like a log'), and ch 18 records that as her first lie told to protect someone else.; ch 24: In ch 17 Neela gives her only knife, the plain six-inch guild knife, to Devan and lays it on his side of the sword (F399). In ch 24 Devan thinks of her asleep 'with her knife under the mattress'. In ch 25 she runs down the stair with 'the plain guild knife in her hand', and in ch 26 it is in her belt. No scene shows the knife going back to her.; ch 7: Ch 7 says Unni is 'not much past twenty'. In ch 12, Asha's slate lists Unni among the recruits she wrote down in her first month at the fort, which was about nine years ago (she arrived at 19 and died at 22, six years ago). That would make him a recruit at about eleven.; ch 11: Ch 11 has Neela recall that Janu said 'He used to have a partner' 'in the first week, over the supper pots.' In ch 3 Janu said it at the lip of the kalari pit during the tour.; ch 16: Ch 16 says Neela 'had missed it twice already, the fever night and the night of the narrows', meaning the cup at the meeting stone. In ch 14 she dragged a late scent-mark across the cup on her way back from the narrows. In ch 18 Ammu counts bare cups without the narrows night ('Three nights... Four, if I count the night of the fever').

3 major continuity errors remain after 1 fix round(s): ch 5: Devan never lies to Neela (bible fixed trait). In ch5 he tells her 'I have to see Bhaskaran about the gate', and the narration then says 'It was not true.'; ch 8: Devan gives Neela 'Oil' as his reason for sending Raiu away, and the narration flatly says 'It did not save oil.' That makes the answer a lie to Neela, which breaks his fixed trait. It should read as a true but evasive answer, like 'Rain'.; ch 32: Ch32 says Devan locked the palace gift away because he distrusted the council and 'never once thought to distrust the gift'. In ch6 he says aloud 'I don't trust gifts from the palace', bans the set from their chamber, and keeps the queen's seal in his sleeve.
